question: A manager asks Claude to pull figures from several uploaded reports into one table and plans to paste it straight into a board deck. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) A tidy table hides which report each number came from and which ones were inferred rather than read.
B) The table will be formatted in a way the presentation software cannot display neatly on a slide.
C) The table will contain more rows than a board audience can reasonably absorb during a meeting.
D) Building the table will use up rather more of her allowance than reading the reports herself would have.
correct_answers: A) A tidy table hides which report each number came from and which ones were inferred rather than read.
explanations: Correct. Putting figures in a grid strips away their provenance and any caveats, so numbers of very different reliability end up looking equally authoritative to the board.
Incorrect. Layout problems are visible immediately and take minutes to correct, unlike a wrong figure nobody notices.
Incorrect. Too much detail is an editing problem, and it is easily fixed once someone reads the table.
Incorrect. The cost of producing the table is minor compared with a board decision resting on untraceable figures.
